title: Maximum Subarray Sum
summary: Find the largest sum of any contiguous, non-empty run of elements.
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray (containing **at least one** element)
with the largest sum, and return that sum.

examples.explanation: The subarray must be non-empty, so the best choice is [-1].

hints: Suppose you know the best sum of a subarray that ends at index i - 1. When does it stop being worth extending that subarray to include nums[i]?
If the running sum ending just before i is negative, it can only drag nums[i] down, so start fresh at nums[i]. Track the best value seen anywhere along the way (this is Kadane's algorithm).

best = nums[0]
current = nums[0]
for i from 1 to n - 1:
    current = max(nums[i], current + nums[i])
    best = max(best, current)
return best

Checking every subarray is O(n^2) (or O(n^3) when re-summing each one). Kadane's algorithm keeps `current`, the best sum of a subarray ending exactly here, which is either nums[i] alone or nums[i] added to the previous best, and records the maximum. One pass: O(n) time, O(1) space. Initializing both values to nums[0] rather than 0 is what makes all-negative arrays come out right.
